proof_summary: Wilson’s theorem factors \((p_{k+1}-1)!\) to show that \(p_k!\equiv1\pmod{p_{k+1}}\) is equivalent to the intervening product being \(1\); when the prime gap is two this product is empty, while otherwise it is exactly the stated exceptional condition. A finite prime count identifies the primes at the exceptional index as \(7841\) and \(7853\), and direct modular computation shows their intervening product is \(1\pmod{7853}\).
